analysis.title: Instacart (CART): Framing Our Company Thesis Following Press Reports Around M&A
key_insights: Press reports say Instacart management has held preliminary conversations with industry participants, including DoorDash and Uber, about a potential sale of the company. GS takes no view on the likelihood of an announcement or a transaction.
GS keeps its Buy rating and $65 12-month price target on CART (unchanged), 15.2% above the $56.44 close of 23 Oct 2026.
Long-term thesis rests on online grocery, which GS sees in the early innings with significant white space, and on retail media advertising as a growth area within digital advertising.
GS says CART has a higher average order value ($110 in 2025) than other delivery players and is anchored more on weekly grocery orders than on convenience or add-on purchases.
GS argues investors underappreciate CART's positioning as a grocery enablement platform across 1P and 3P transactions, enterprise software and retailer enablement tools.
At GS's Communacopia + Technology conference in September, management said GTV growth has stayed in the low teens for several quarters, an acceleration relative to 2025 trends.

Management framed the Clementine AI grocery assistant as a way to personalize the consumer experience and raise basket sizes, and said price parity with in-store prices benefits consumers and retailers.
Advertising momentum has been solid for several quarters, driven by ecosystem innovation, extended reach through Carrot Ads and diversification of supply and demand.
DoorDash (Deliveroo, Wolt) and Uber (DHER, ezCater) have completed other deals that point to industry consolidation. Both have said publicly that the bar for M&A remains high.
GS carries an M&A rank of 3 for CART (0%-15% probability of becoming a target), which is immaterial and not factored into the price target.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and $65 target unchanged after M&A press reports. The target blends 14.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA on NTM+1 estimates with a modified DCF at 18.0x EV/FCF-SBC on NTM+4 estimates.

earnings_insights: GS estimates for CART: 2026E revenue $4,247.7mn, EBITDA $1,295.1mn, EPS $2.26. 2027E revenue $4,775.2mn, EBITDA $1,473.5mn, EPS $2.70. Full-year 2025 figures: revenue $3,742.0mn, EBITDA $1,086.0mn, EPS $1.61.
Quarterly EPS: 6/26 $0.45 (as listed in the table, not labeled as reported or estimate). GS estimates 9/26E $0.61, 12/26E $0.65 and 3/27E $0.68.
risk_factors: Uncertainty around near-term order growth as customer behavior normalizes post-pandemic, with slowing grocery inflation and lower government benefits.
Questions about normalized medium-term GTV growth.
Market share and competitive intensity versus traditional grocers (larger orders) and on-demand delivery platforms (smaller orders).
Customer concentration, including possible declining pricing power and retailers sourcing more orders themselves over time.
Cadence of advertising revenue growth, where a slower ramp would be downside to revenue and profit.
Overhang from expiration of lock-ups on employee shares.
Volatility from the global macro environment and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
